item_name: STRAIGHT-IN (FLAPS LDG, FLAPS UP, FLAPS Τ/Ο).

observations.text: SP planned and flew the straight-in approach to the desired standard for this Training Section, with the IP nominating the point at which the A/C was placed on the runway extension and executing part of the configuration change. Final airspeed reached 22 knots above the computed value and the A/C was 380 feet above the desired glide path before the IP's corrections, and alignment with the runway center line was achieved only inside 0.5 NM. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent planning of the five NM point and completion of the A/C configuration prior to 2 NM are expected to develop over the following sorties.

SP planned the approach and placed the A/C at five NM on the runway extension without the IP directing or executing any part of the sequence, requiring verbal indications only for the landing check and the standardized reports. The A/C configuration was completed at 2 NM, final airspeed was held 15 knots above the computed value and never below it, and the deviation from the desired glide path reached 300 feet high. Alignment with the runway center line was established at 0.5 NM, and all deviations were recognized and corrected with delay after the IP's verbal indications. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned and flew the straight-in approach according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual without any verbal prompting, obtaining the ATC clearance in a timely manner and executing clearing during the approach. Final airspeed reached 12 knots above the computed value and the deviation from the desired glide path 230 feet high, with alignment on the runway center line established at 1 NM. The deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, and the required checks and the standardized reports were completed prior to 2 NM. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned the approach accurately and promptly, bringing the A/C to five NM at the runway extension ready to configure for final and completing the configuration well prior to 2 NM within the published landing gear and flap limitations. Final airspeed was contained within 8 knots above the computed value and never below it, the deviation from the desired glide path within 130 feet, and the A/C was aligned with the runway center line at 1.5 NM. The ATC clearance was obtained in a timely manner, clearing was executed throughout the approach and all the standardized reports were given at the correct points. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned and flew the straight-in approach with exceptional precision in the landing flap, flaps up and take-off flap configurations, arriving at five NM on the runway extension already prepared to configure for final. Deviations were negligible, within 3 knots above the computed final airspeed and never below it and within 40 feet of the desired glide path, and the A/C was aligned with the runway center line at 2.5 NM. Clearing was continuous, the ATC clearance was requested and read back correctly, and the required checks and standardized reports were given in full without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a descent plan computed without allowance for the tailwind on the runway extension, did not arrive at five NM ready to configure for final and did not complete the A/C configuration prior to 2 NM. Final airspeed was allowed to decay 10 knots below the computed value while the landing gear and the flaps were selected late, with the result that the IP directed the power correction and executed part of the configuration change. The A/C was 400 feet above the desired glide path at 2 NM and was aligned with the runway center line only inside 0.4 NM.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not perform the required landing check and did not obtain the ATC clearance in a timely manner, so the straight-in was continued without a clearance until the IP intervened. Final airspeed reached 25 knots above the computed value with the landing gear selected close to its limiting airspeed, and the deviation from the desired glide path reached 420 feet high. The IP directed the corrections and executed the alignment with the runway center line, which had not been established by 0.5 NM.

SP planned and flew the straight-in approach to the desired standard for this Training Section, completing the A/C configuration and the required checks after the IP's verbal indications. Final airspeed was held 15 knots above the computed value and never below it, the deviation from the desired glide path reached 300 feet high and alignment with the runway center line was established at 0.5 NM, all recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier planning of the five NM point and recognition of the glide path deviation without prompting are expected to improve.

SP planned the straight-in approach and completed the A/C configuration prior to 2 NM without the IP's verbal indications, giving the standardized reports at the correct points. Final airspeed reached 13 knots above the computed value and the deviation from the desired glide path 240 feet high, with the A/C aligned on the runway center line at 1.1 NM. The deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, and the landing gear and flap limitations were respected throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned the approach so that the A/C arrived at five NM at the runway extension ready to configure, and completed the configuration prior to 2 NM within the published landing gear and flap limitations. Final airspeed was contained within 7 knots above the computed value and never below it, the deviation from the desired glide path within 140 feet, and alignment with the runway center line was established at 1.6 NM. The required checks were performed accurately and promptly and the standardized reports were given without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP computed the final airspeed for the landing flap, flaps up and take-off flap configurations before the approach and flew each straight-in with exceptional accuracy, configuring the A/C well clear of the gear and flap limiting airspeeds. Deviations were negligible, within 2 knots above the computed final airspeed and never below it and within 50 feet of the desired glide path, with the A/C aligned on the runway center line at 3 NM. Clearing was continuous throughout the approach and all the required checks and standardized reports were completed before 2 NM. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a power and pitch technique that was not adjusted for the flaps up configuration, did not perform the maneuver according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual and allowed the final airspeed to fall 12 knots below the computed value. The deviation from the desired glide path reached 350 feet low at 2 NM, with the result that the IP directed the go around and executed part of the recovery. The required landing check was completed only after the IP nominated the remaining items.

SP, due to a failure to call the go around after the deviations from the desired glide path had exceeded the limits of the approach, did not execute the go around in time and continued the straight-in with the A/C 400 feet high at 2 NM. Final airspeed reached 24 knots above the computed value and the A/C had not been aligned with the runway center line by 0.5 NM, with the result that the IP called and executed the go around. The standardized reports were given only after the IP nominated them.

SP, due to late selection of the landing gear and flaps, did not complete the A/C configuration prior to 2 NM and intercepted the desired glide path late. Final airspeed was 15 knots above the computed value and the deviation from the desired glide path reached 300 feet high, corrected only after the IP's verbal indications. Alignment with the runway center line was established at 0.5 NM, recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to inadequate monitoring of airspeed during the approach, did not maintain the computed final airspeed while configuring the A/C for the landing flap straight-in, and the required landing check was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts. Final airspeed was 15 knots above the computed value and the deviation from the desired glide path reached 200 feet low, recognized and corrected with delay. Alignment with the runway center line was achieved at 0.5 NM.

SP planned and flew the straight-in approach within the desired standards, obtaining the ATC clearance in a timely manner and completing the A/C configuration prior to 2 NM without the IP's intervention. Final airspeed reached 12 knots above the computed value and the deviation from the desired glide path 220 feet high, twice recognized and corrected in a timely manner, with alignment on the runway center line established at 1 NM. Marginal performance for the Training Section - closer control of the final airspeed and earlier alignment with the runway center line are expected to improve.

SP planned the approach so that the A/C arrived at five NM at the runway extension ready to configure for final, obtaining the ATC clearance in a timely manner and executing clearing throughout the approach. Final airspeed was held within 6 knots above the computed value and never below it, the deviation from the desired glide path within 120 feet, and the A/C was aligned with the runway center line at 1.5 NM. The configuration was completed prior to 2 NM in accordance with the landing gear and flap limitations, and the required checks were performed accurately and promptly. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned and flew the straight-in approach with exceptional precision, computing the final airspeed for the landing flap, flaps up and take-off flap configurations before the approach and arriving at five NM at the runway extension ready to configure. Deviations were negligible, within 3 knots above the computed final airspeed and never below it and within 45 feet of the desired glide path, and the A/C was aligned with the runway center line at 2.5 NM. The A/C was configured with a wide margin to the gear and flap limiting airspeeds, clearing was continuous and every standardized report was given in full and on time. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to the use of the runway threshold instead of the computed aim point as the visual reference on final, did not perform the maneuver according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual and allowed the A/C to descend below the desired glide path. The deviation reached 320 feet low with the final airspeed 8 knots below the computed value in the landing flap configuration, with the result that the IP directed the go around and executed part of the recovery. The landing check was completed only after the IP nominated the remaining items.

SP, due to an attention bottleneck on the preceding traffic at the expense of the instrument cross-check, did not monitor the final airspeed and the desired glide path during the straight-in and did not give the standardized reports. Final airspeed decayed 10 knots below the computed value and the A/C was 380 feet below the desired glide path at 2 NM, with the result that the IP directed the power correction and executed the level off. Alignment with the runway center line had not been established by 0.5 NM.

SP, due to a drift correction that did not account for the crosswind on the runway extension, did not align the A/C with the runway center line at the required distance and did not complete the A/C configuration prior to 2 NM. Alignment was established only at 0.5 NM after the IP's verbal indications, with the final airspeed 15 knots above the computed value and the deviation from the desired glide path 300 feet high. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, did not perform the required landing check in the prescribed sequence and did not give the standardized reports until the IP nominated them. Final airspeed reached 15 knots above the computed value and the deviation from the desired glide path 200 feet low, with alignment on the runway center line established at 0.5 NM. All deviations were recognized and corrected with delay after the IP's verbal indications.

SP, due to a power setting retained too high after the landing flaps were selected, did not maintain the computed final airspeed on the straight-in approach, although the A/C configuration was completed prior to 2 NM and the required checks were performed. Final airspeed reached 13 knots above the computed value and the deviation from the desired glide path 230 feet high, and the A/C was aligned with the runway center line at 1 NM. The deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to an incomplete mental model of the approach sequence that was not updated when the ATC clearance changed the landing runway, did not plan the approach so that the A/C arrived at five NM at the new runway extension ready to configure for final. The configuration was completed at 2 NM, final airspeed reached 12 knots above the computed value and the deviation from the desired glide path 240 feet high, with the A/C aligned on the runway center line at 1 NM. The deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP planned and flew the straight-in approach accurately and promptly, arriving at five NM at the runway extension ready to configure and completing the configuration prior to 2 NM; however, the final airspeed twice reached 9 knots above the computed value. The deviation from the desired glide path remained within 145 feet and alignment with the runway center line was established at 1.5 NM, and the required checks and the standardized reports were completed without prompting. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the final airspeed and earlier alignment with the runway center line are expected to improve.

SP planned and flew the straight-in approach with exceptional precision in the landing flap, flaps up and take-off flap configurations, computing the final airspeed for each and arriving at five NM at the runway extension ready to configure. Deviations were negligible, within 2 knots above the computed final airspeed and never below it and within 35 feet of the desired glide path, and the A/C was aligned with the runway center line at 3 NM. When the preceding traffic did not clear the runway, the go around was initiated in time and flown correctly without hesitation, and all the standardized reports were given in full. Above end of block MIF achieved.
